The transformation removes padding and maps the two standard Base64 symbols to the URL-safe alphabet before dot-joining the three components. RFC 7515 requires these protected-header, payload, and signature components to use unpadded Base64URL. The contract covers this output mapping only; it does not claim DPoP claim validity, key custody, or server acceptance.

sites.rationale: The helper Base64-encodes SHA-256(code_verifier), removes padding, and maps the standard alphabet to the URL-safe alphabet before the challenge is sent in an OAuth authorization request. RFC 7636 requires the S256 code challenge to be BASE64URL(SHA256(ASCII(code_verifier))) and defines base64url without padding. The contract covers this output mapping only; it does not claim verifier entropy, state generation, server enforcement, or CSRF correctness.
